title: デジタル通信と信号処理
subtitle: Digital Communications and Signal Processing
keywords: Discrete time signal and frequency characteristics 2.z-transform and transfer function 3.Sampling theorem 4.Discrete Fourier transform and FFT 5.Modulation/demodulation and multiple access
educationalGoal: Analog signals such as voice, music, images, and video are digitized and processed. Digital signal processing can be implemented as a computer program, which enables flexible and complex processing. In this course, students will learn the basics of digital signal processing by digitizing analog signals such as audio and video. They will also learn the basics of digital communications achieved by digital signal processing.
advice: Students will systematically learn the following basic knowledge and theory about digital signal processing and digital communication: 1. Discrete time signals and systems. 2. Frequency characteristics of discrete-time systems. 3. z-transform and transfer function. 4. Sampling theorem. 5. Discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and fast Fourier transform (FFT). 6. Digital filter design method. 7. Baseband transmission, modulation/demodulation and multiple access.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of the basics of mathematics such as exponential functions, trigonometric functions, complex numbers, and linear algebra is required. It is desirable that students have knowledge of probability statistics, Fourier transform, and Laplace transform. These are introduced in this course. Numerical calculation software such as Excel are used in the practices.

activityGoals.body: Understand and apply the convolution sum and frequency characteristics of discrete-time signals.
Understand and apply the relationship between z-transform, the transfer function and circuit.
Understand and apply the sampling theorem.
Understand and apply DFT and its fast calculation method.
Understand the basics of digital filter design.
Understand the basics of modulation/demodulation and multiple access.
